baseline_note: Independent source comparison completed against the selected Characters third-printing and Campaigns fourth-printing baseline; detailed evidence is recorded in docs/gurps-equipment-source-review.md.

sections.omitted_rows: Explicit non-catalog rows: Punch, Kick, Kick with Boots, Blunt Teeth, Fangs, Sharp Beak, Sharp Teeth and Striker are natural attacks. Brass Knuckles lacks a table ST value. Stun Gun and Garrote use damage forms outside this row set. Force Sword, Monowire Whip, Chainsaw, and the seven purchased Whip lengths retain their exact table values and typed special procedures.
No scoped table row is omitted; independently owned mechanics outside issues #685, #702, and #703 remain explicitly dispositioned elsewhere.

The eight selected simple body rows are the executable subset. Every other B283-286 row is itemized in armor-split-dr, including simple-location pieces, advanced suits and horse barding; generic split-DR, facing, layering and reaction-penalty behavior is implemented without inventing the omitted inventory rows.

No fixed-TL physical B288 item or embedded purchasable variant is omitted. Piton is an alias for the recorded Iron Spike rather than another item. Typed fuel, cold-protection, electronics and task effects execute through the shared resource procedures.

B264-266 Starting Wealth and B267 Legality Class are bound to the existing economics and jurisdiction services rather than physical equipment rows. Other B264-270 campaign and weapon rules remain separately dispositioned; no price band or LC is invented on a selected item.
No scoped table row is omitted; independently owned mechanics outside issues #685, #702, and #703 remain explicitly dispositioned elsewhere.

The Light Cloak and Heavy Cloak appearances duplicate physical rows already recorded from B276. Force Shield has no finite HP and therefore records its hardened DR on the shield profile. Shield-rush execution is transferred to child issue #714; cloak entangling remains accounted separately.
No scoped table row is omitted; independently owned mechanics outside issues #685, #702, and #703 remain explicitly dispositioned elsewhere.

B283 low-tech omissions: Fur Loincloth, Fur Tunic, Bronze Breastplate, Cloth Armor, Leather Jacket, Mail Hauberk, Mail Shirt, Double Mail Hauberk, Steel Breastplate, Buff Coat; Bronze Armbands/Greaves, Cloth Sleeves, Heavy Leather Leggings/Sleeves, Leather Leggings/Pants, Studded Leather Skirt, Mail Leggings/Sleeves, Scale Leggings/Sleeves, Heavy Plate Arms/Legs, Plate Arms/Legs; Bronze Helmet/Pot-Helm, Cloth/Leather Cap, Leather Helm, Legionary Helmet, Mail Coif, Barrel Helm, Face Mask, Greathelm, Pot-Helm; Cloth/Leather Gloves, Gauntlets, Heavy Gauntlets; Sandals, Shoes, Boots and Sollerets. B284-285 omissions: Flak Jacket, Frag/Ballistic/Tactical Vest and inserts/plates, Ballistic/Tactical Suit, Reinforced/Assault Boots, Ballistic Gloves, Gas Mask, Steel Pot, Frag/Ballistic Helmet and visors, NBC/Space/Vacc Suit and helmets, Battlesuit, Combat Hardsuit and Space Armor with helmets. B286 omissions are every named Leather-and-Cloth, Mail, Scale and Plate horse face, head/neck, partial/full barding and legging row. Generic split/front DR, layering and reaction effects are implemented; unselected inventory rows, suit systems, add-ons and mount anatomy remain explicit omissions.
No scoped table row is omitted; independently owned mechanics outside issues #685, #702, and #703 remain explicitly dispositioned elsewhere.

No B289 weapon-accessory item is omitted. Every row is recorded with fixed inventory facts and a typed actor- or weapon-bound effect; target validation, attachment and lanyard retrieval use the shared resource ledger.

No B289 physical row is omitted. Skill-relative medical/laboratory rows preserve their printed variable TL, and the seven named portable tool-kit variants preserve their individual TL, cost, weight and task binding. Transportation is a cross-reference, not an equipment row.

footnotes.behaviour: An unbalanced weapon cannot parry in the same turn it was used to attack.
A fencing weapon takes a smaller cumulative penalty for repeated parries.
A weapon marked unready after an attack must be readied before its next use.
Attacking below a weapon's minimum ST applies its skill and defence penalty.
A damage armor divisor reduces the target's DR before penetration is computed.
Tight-beam burning damage may target the eyes and vitals that other non-penetrating damage cannot.
A thrown weapon leaves the thrower's inventory and is the projectile itself.
Only thrown or explicitly blockable projectiles may be blocked or parried.
A per-round reload loads one shot at a time instead of exchanging a magazine.
Rate of fire and recoil together bound how many shots of a burst can hit.
A full-automatic-only firearm requires at least one-quarter of its listed RoF, rounded up, or every remaining round when fewer remain.
A RoF 5+ weapon may attack ordered targets within one 30-degree angle, spending traversal shots and adding one to effective Recoil per successive target.
A RoF 5+ weapon prepays fire into exact mapped zones and automatically attacks anyone entering a zone or its firing swath before the firer's next turn.
A variable-power scope adds up to its bonus as aiming seconds accumulate.
A fixed-power scope grants its bonus only after its full aiming time.
One-handed bracing and bipod bracing each add their own aiming bonus.
A ready shield adds its defence bonus and may be used to block once per turn.
An item carries its own HP, DR and HT and can be damaged and disabled.
A container limits the weight it can hold, in the same explicit weight unit.
Carried equipment weight selects the encumbrance level that caps Move and Dodge.
A weapon's parry column may add or subtract from the computed parry score.
A two-handed weapon occupies both hands and cannot share them with a shield.
A melee table row marked as throwable also requires its independently listed muscle-powered ranged mode before the physical item can be selected.
An impaling pick can become stuck and requires a separate attempt to free it.
Flails penalize attempts to parry or block them, with smaller penalties for a nunchaku.
A lance uses the mounted-charge damage procedure when wielded from a moving mount.
A weapon with starred variable reach requires the table's reach-change handling rather than freely selecting any listed reach.
A double-dagger weapon becomes unready after attacking unless the wielder has at least 1.5 times its listed ST.
A cutlass hilt acts as brass knuckles in close combat.
A caret technology level is a setting-dependent superscience designation, not an integer technology level.

footnotes.behaviour: Some melee rows add a die expression to ST-based damage rather than a fixed integer modifier.
Whip minimum ST, cost and weight vary with the purchased maximum reach.
Fuel-burning gear consumes a fuel supply over time.
Insulated gear modifies cold environment exposure while it is in use.
Battery-powered computing gear runs tasks while charge remains.
Gyroc rockets inflict one-third damage at 1-2 yards, one-half damage at 3-10 yards, and full damage beyond 10 yards.
A rechargeable power cell holds shots as charge, not as disposable rounds; the existing per-round ammunition implementation must not be reused for it.
A smartgun electronically restricts or assists the authorised user.
A weapon whose hit also imposes a linked affliction resisted separately.
Surge damage interacts with electrical targets differently from ordinary burning.
Beam attacks lose effect to environmental obscurants and intervening conditions.
One armor row grants lower DR against its explicitly named damage type.
One armor row protects only one facing of the locations it covers.
Armor worn over other armor combines DR and applies the printed DX penalty for each extra non-head layer.
Visible or discovered armor applies the printed cumulative reaction penalty.

Opt-in conventional TL5+ repeating firearms and revolvers: malfunction precedence, misfire/stoppage/mechanical state, diagnosis, clearing and repair. Low-TL explosions, beam weapons, grenades and explosive ammunition remain outside this protocol.

footnotes.behaviour: Shells are conserved independently from dispersed-projectile effective RoF; at less than 10% of 1/2D, shell RoF is retained while damage dice, adds and target DR use half the projectile multiplier rounded down.
Ammunition types change damage, damage type, armor divisor and cost per round.
A penetrating blowpipe hit can carry a selected poison or drug follow-up.
A cloak, bolas, lariat or net hit resolves an authored binding instead of ordinary table damage.
An atlatl changes a dart or javelin throw without becoming the projectile itself.
A goat's-foot lever permits a stronger crossbow to be reloaded with extra Ready maneuvers.
A pistol crossbow uses two hands to ready but one hand to attack while retaining rated weapon ST.
A shield can be damaged, destroyed, or used as cover rather than only as a bonus.
Ordinary shields may bash and carry a damage-increasing spike.
An ordinary shield may rush through the Slam procedure; bucklers and force shields may not.
A buckler uses its own Shield specialty and has distinct ready, drop, hand-occupation, and rush rules.
Iron and plastic-riot shield variants alter cost, weight, DR, HP, and available TL without changing DB.
A heavy weapon requires a crew, a mount and setup time before it can fire.
Guided and homing heavy-weapon missiles acquire and attack through distinct aiming procedures.
Selected launchers cannot attack inside their printed minimum range.
A launcher attack creates a burning-damage hazard behind the firer.
Heavy-weapon ammunition carries a separately resolved explosive and fragmentation payload.

footnotes.reference: B281 Heavy Weapon Table and note 5
footnotes.behaviour: Mounted weapons and detachable tripods change handling, setup and carried weight.
Under-barrel and integral launchers inherit handling from their host weapon.
A flamethrower projects a sustained burning stream rather than discrete rapid-fire shots.
Fixed and skill-relative TL variants preserve their distinct availability, weight, cost and task bindings.
Accessories attach to a weapon and change its handling or accuracy.
Ordinary tools grant task or skill effects rather than combat values.
A weapon's bulk determines how easily it can be carried concealed.
A normally two-handed firearm may be fired one-handed at 1.5 times listed ST, but becomes unready unless the wielder has three times listed ST.
A row's legality class governs where it may lawfully be carried.
Starting wealth and cost of living bound what equipment a character may buy.
A weapon's quality decides whether a critical miss breaks it and whether a resistant weapon gets a second roll; a broken weapon loses readiness.

bindings.detail: Every mechanically supported Basic Set row has a matching implemented equipment definition and source in the pinned Characters package. EquipmentCatalog.bind returns exactly that supported subset; rows with declared unsupported mechanics remain audit-only and cannot produce inventory specs.

The Lite sample rows cite sjg:gurps-lite-4e-2004, which the Lite package does declare, but no pinned package registers equipment:broadsword or equipment:leather-armor, so the Lite sample cannot bind either.

lite_gaps.detail: Only one Lite weapon row (broadsword) is recorded. The remaining Lite weapon rows, including every ranged row, are absent from LITE_EQUIPMENT.
Only one Lite armor row (leather armor) is recorded, and its covered locations differ from the Basic Set row of the same name; neither has been reconciled.
No Lite general equipment, container or ammunition row is recorded, so Lite inventory play has no audited gear beyond the two sample rows.
The exact Lite revision was not available for inspection, so no Lite row, unit or price is source-verified and every Lite provenance record stays pending.
